**Finding: compliant (no redline proposed).**

The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Tri City, so the preferred playbook position is satisfied:

- **Article 3 (Appointment)** creates no exclusivity, sole-source or minimum-volume commitment; M&I is simply appointed to perform the Services.
- **Articles 10, 11, 16.2, 17, 21, 22** contain no covenant limiting the businesses we may operate, the providers we may engage, or products we may build or buy; confidentiality in 17.3–17.4 is mutual and information-based only.
- The two use limitations found are **licence-scope terms on M&I's own deliverables**, not restrictions on our business: §21.7(B) (use M&I's Services for our internal business purposes; no resale of those Services) and §23.5 (escrowed source code for our own internal processing; no sublicense/service-bureau use). Neither prevents us from developing internally, using alternative providers, or competing with M&I, so they sit outside this rule's boundary.
- **§21.11(A)** expressly contemplates our acquisition of additional financial institutions, which roll into the definition of "Customer" — no acquisition constraint.

No walk-away exposure: there is no post-term restriction of any duration and no undefined "competing business" scope. Accordingly I recorded this as compliant at the preferred level and did not redline.
